outline.rationale: The user is new to neural networks but targeting the original Transformer paper, so I build from zero: node 1 establishes the neural network machinery (neurons, weights, layers, training) that everything else assumes. Node 2 covers embeddings since the paper takes vectorized tokens as given. Node 3 motivates the architecture (RNN/sequence limitations) so the paper's framing makes sense. Nodes 4-5 tackle attention itself—the paper's core—split into the single-head mechanism and the multi-head extension to keep them MECE. Node 6 covers the encoder-decoder organization, and node 7 sweeps up the remaining components the paper stacks around attention (positional encoding, FFN, residuals, layer norm) so they aren't a surprise. Node 8 is a synthesis/reading-guide node that directly serves the stated goal by mapping concepts to paper sections and notation. I deliberately excluded training pipelines, framework code, and hands-on implementation per the deprioritization, and kept intuition-first framing throughout.
